chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Alawi, from al-'Amraki, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a Bukhti camel that became sexually frenzied and killed a man: what is upon its owner? He said: «The blood-money is upon him.»

key_terms.اغْتَلَمَ: became sexually frenzied or violently excited
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: the prescribed blood-money compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.بُخْتِيٍّ: a Bukhti camel, a type of camel referred to in the case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a camel kills a man—does the owner have to pay diyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability when an animal kills a person. It states that the owner is responsible for paying the diyah in the case described, establishing a principle of financial accountability for harm caused by one's animal.
